title: Gulia M
content: Before my body put itself into a coma following extremely violent status epilepticus, detected late when I was already experiencing cerebral hypoxia (blue skin), I had been hospitalized for a week for a procedure called SEEG. This procedure involves inserting electrodes to perform an intracranial EEG to determine the location of the epileptic foci. The final step of this SEEG is for the neurologist to send electrical discharges via a machine via these intracranial electrodes to observe the brain's reactions. Following this, that same evening, I suffered this state of illness with countless seizures. I was transferred to intensive care in a coma. This coma lasted two days. This is what I experienced; even if words are not enough to explain it. So, basically, because the experience I had is indescribable. I was in reality in a coma, unconscious, but what I experienced was quite different. I crossed a small wooden bridge that went over a gently flowing river; and I arrived at a path with an embankment and tall, magnificent trees. The Earth itself was magnificent, and there was an extraordinarily beautiful, but not dazzling, light coming through the trees. One of my deceased dogs was walking beside me, peacefully. All the colors were splendid; it was so magnificent that it's indescribable. I felt a total serenity that you can't feel on earth; I was outside of time; time didn't exist. I knew I was me and that the situation was special, but I didn't feel any surprise or questioning; it was simply normal. I was part of a whole, in a harmony that was once again indescribable. It could have lasted the length of a walk, or I don't know what eternity was, because there was no time, just the present moment; it was so magnificent. The words I'm using aren't the right ones; you can't understand it if you haven't experienced it; there are no words beautiful and powerful enough to describe this journey. The little wooden bridge and the water were so magical, as were the path and the earth of the embankment, as well as the trees and the light. My dog, although deceased, who was walking beside me, didn't question me; we just walked peacefully together, in complete inner peace. I wasn't aware that I was actually in the hospital and in a coma. I was fully in the present moment, with no past or future coming to mind, just this landscape of which I was a part, like a greater whole. I was so serene, I had become serenity, it was as if it had invaded my entire universe and guided every beat of my heart. It was so magnificent, but it was like that, as if it were self-evident, and I was too busy living and being life. It was as I was looking at this extraordinary land that I began to hear all the beeping of the machines around me, and to feel the pain of the tubes bothering me, and to see the bright, aggressive lights of the intensive care unit. My hands were tied; apparently, I was very agitated in my coma. I gradually realized that I was in the hospital. Shortly after, my loved ones told me about that horrible moment of the Exetera coma. Yet, all I could think about was that landscape, light, and serenity. I had so much happiness, although the word happiness isn't a strong enough word for what I felt. But I've always been surrounded by family and friends who are very rational and resistant to such inexplicable things, and I quickly understood that they didn't believe me and that I shouldn't talk about it. Even I came to doubt it. I never doubted that I'd experienced an NDE, but I told myself that maybe it didn't mean anything after all, even if that memory would remain extraordinary for the rest of my life. However, although I have this doubt, I doubt it, that is to say, I tell myself now, much more than before, that anything is possible, and that I was probably wrong to doubt it. I no longer see the end of life as nothingness; I think there's probably something beyond it. An afterlife. I wouldn't say I believe in God, but more in the universe or something like that. However, I can't be sure; I continue to doubt.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: Uncertain, Illness, Life threatening event, but not clinical death
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: More consciousness and alertness than normal, The questions don't seem very representative of my experience, so it's hard to answer. I wouldn't say it was about consciousness or alertness, but rather the magic of beauty, serenity, and the present moment.
elements.At what time during the experience were: I'm not sure I understand if this refers to consciousness and alertness during the NDE. If so, my consciousness and alertness were at their highest level throughout the entire experience.
elements.Did time seem to speed up or slow down?: Everything seemed to be happening at once; or time stopped or lost all meaning, Time didn't exist. There was no past or future; only the present moment existed.
elements.Please compare your vision during the ex: In my case, what can I say? Right before the experience, I was in my hospital bed before losing consciousness. I was far from imagining what was about to happen.
elements.Please compare your hearing during the e: I didn't experience anything unusual with my hearing, neither silence nor any particular noise. It's hard to describe; it was just life, and I was life. That's how it was.
elements.Did you encounter or become aware of any: Yes, It was my second dog, a golden retriever who had passed away a few years earlier. She was walking beside me. I was very happy to see her but didn't question it. We walked together in indescribable happiness.
elements.Did you see an unearthly light?: Yes, The light was so bright without being blinding. It was shining through the trees and making the trees even more beautiful. It was a light of love and magic.
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: At the same time, it felt normal and almost obvious. But, I was also in awe of the purity of the landscape and everything in it. I knew I was part of it all in perfect harmony. I was happy to see my dog again while finding it completely normal. Overall, I felt an extraordinary serenity, a immense sense of being outside of time and fully present, a kind of paradisaical happiness.
elements.Did you feel a sense of harmony or unity: I felt united or one with the world
elements.Have your religious practices changed si: Uncertain, I'm more interested in Buddhism and especially in the present moment
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was entirely not consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience, I was agnostic, but at the same time, I thought there might be some meaning to the universe that could exist in life and death.
elements.Did you have a change in your values and: Yes, It reinforced my idea that the universe has an impact on our lives; and that other forms of animal or plant life have an intelligence and goodness that we don't yet understand
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, As I mentioned, some questions don't allow me to answer precisely. Since the experience, I've felt more able to empathize with animals or nature. Although this remains just an impression without certainty.
Uncertain, I wouldn't say specific information or love, but the experience made me realize afterward that such inner peace was possible.
elements.What life changes occurred in your life: Notably, I have more sensitivity towards animals and nature. I also have greater open-mindedness
elements.Was the experience difficult to express: Yes, Someone on Earth who hasn't experienced it cannot understand what it's about. Words are not strong enough to express this experience.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience more accurately than other life events that occurred around the time of the experience, My NDE is so incredible that it's impossible to forget. Of course, I also remember the trauma at the hospital; the physical and emotional pain, etc. But the hospital memory doesn't erase my indelible memory of that extraordinary moment; unlike anything else in my earthly life.
elements.Are there one or several parts of your e: Serenity and inner peace, the present moment, extraordinary nature
elements.Did you have any knowledge of near death: Uncertain, I knew it existed but I didn't know much more about it
elements.What did you believe about the reality o: Experience was probably real, I knew it was real, but my loved ones who didn't believe me made me really doubt the reality of my experience.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was probably real, I know I experienced it and it was definitely an NDE. But as long as there's no scientific validation, I think I'll continue to doubt life after life
elements.At any time in your life, has anything e: Uncertain, I'd say this extraordinary landscape vaguely resembles one of the walks I took with my deceased dog. Although, in reality, it doesn't resemble it at all. It was so much more beautiful and so different.
elements.Is there anything else that you would li: I'd love for it to be scientifically proven so I can finally be sure that I got a glimpse of life after life. If that's the case, then I could almost say that death is good news
elements.Did the questions asked and information: No, The questions weren't always relevant to my experience. I hesitated on some answers because the wording didn't match what I went through.
